body.p: The Office Action dated August 20, 2024, is received and carefully noted. Claims 1 and 6-9 were pending. In this Amendment, claims 1, 6, and 8-9 are amended and new claim 10 is added. Support for the amendments may be found throughout the specification, for example, in Figure 3 and paragraphs [0017] and [0036] of the specification. After entry of the Amendment, claims 1 and 6-10 are pending in the present application and respectfully submitted for reconsideration in view of the foregoing amendments and the following remarks.

Examiner Hodge is thanked for her courtesies extended during a telephone interview with Applicant's representative on December 4, 2024. During the interview, the Examiner indicates that the amended claims overcome the objection to the specification and the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection stated at pages 2 and 6 of the Office Action, respectively. Further, the terms "processing unit" and "display apparatus" were discussed with regard to the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(f). The Examiner agrees that the term "processing unit" is acceptable. Applicant amends the term "display apparatus" of claims 8 and 9 to "display," as suggested by the Examiner. In addition, the Examiner agreed the amendments to independent claims 1, 8, and 9 distinguish over the cited references, in particular, the primary reference Fujiwara (Japanese Patent Publication No. 2016-214491). The summary of the interview communications is incorporated herein.

Claims 1 and 6-9 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Fujiwara (Japanese Patent Publication No. 2016-214491; hereinafter "Fuji") in view of Pathinarpuothi (NPL "Instantaneous Heart Rate as a Robust Feature for Sleep Apnea Severity Detection using Deep learning" published in 2017; hereinafter "Path") and Zhang (NPL "Sleep Stage Classification Based on Multi-level Feature Learning and Recurrent Neural Networks vis Wearble Device" published in 2017.) Applicants respectfully traverse the obviousness rejection as the cited references, either alone or in combination, fail to disclose or suggest the limitations of the pending
claims.
Independent Claim 1, as amended, recites, among other things, at least the features:

determining whether each of the RRI data is a normal RRI value or an abnormal RRI value based on comparison, instantaneously generating a feature vector . .., wherein the variable length vector does not include the abnormal RRI value, and wherein a number of elements of the variable length vector is variable, not generating the variable length vector if the abnormal RRI value within the RRI data is determined, and inputting the variable length vector . .. as the feature vector to the processing unit operating as a recurrent neural network." Similar features of amended claim 1 are further incorporated into amended claims 8 and 9.

In summary, the claimed subject matter determines whether each of the RRI data is a normal value or an abnormal RRI value based on comparison. An abnormal variable length vector is not inputted to the recurrent neural network. Further, a normal variable length vector, which does not include the abnormal RRI value, is inputted to the recurrent neural network. The normal variable length vector does not include the abnormal RRI value. Each of elements of the normal variable length vector is the normal RRI value and the number of elements of the normal variable length vector is variable.
Applicant respectfully submits that none of Fuji, Path, and Zhang, when taken singly or in combination, teach or suggest the above-identified claimed features.

According to line 11 in page 7 and lines 9-14 in page 8 of the office action, Fuji teaches comparing each of the RRI data to a normal value threshold related to RRI ( 20-processes the RRI data included in the heartbeat data, and changes temporally whether the subject is apnea or hypopnea or normal breathing; ,128-normal RRI variation is less than 50 ms, and NN 50 is an indicator of severe variation), determining whether each of the RRI data is a normal RRI value based on the comparison ( 76-performs the identification of apnea and normal breathing based on RRI data).
Applicant respectfully disagrees with the allegations. Fuji fails to teach or suggest "determining whether each of the RRI data is a normal RRI value or an abnormal RRI value based on

comparison," as recited in amended claims 1, 8, and 9. Please note that RRI data as recited in proposed claims 1, 8, and 9 are INPUT to the recurrent neural network. In Fuji, however, "the identification of apnea and normal breathing" is OUTPUT from a neural network.

Fuji also fails to teach or suggest the features "the variable length vector does not include the abnormal RRI value, and wherein a number of elements of the variable length vector is variable, not generating the variable length vector if the abnormal RRI value within the RRI data is determined," as recited in amended claim 1 and similarly in amended claims 8 and 9.

Path also fails to teach or suggest the above-identified features of amended claim 1, and similar features of amended claims 8 and 9. According to lines 2-17 on page 10 of the office action, Path teaches that wherein the feature vector is a variable number-of-normal-RRI-data vector formed as a time series of a group of pieces of the normal RRI data having normal values respectively indicating the plurality of heart rate intervals in an identification target period having a fixed period length of about 60 seconds (page 294, right col., , 2-this type of stacked LSTM has the capability to learn at various time scales over the given sequence of inputs; page 294, right col., last , -the trained models were independently tested for minute-by-minute apnea classification using the rest of the data from all the classes; page 295, right col., , 2-the LSTM model was able to classify and identify the entire sleep apnea and non-sleep apnea incidence with complete accuracy in datasets (1) and (2)), inputting the variable number-of-normal-RRIdata vector formed as the time series of the group of pieces of the normal RRI data as the feature vector to the processing unit operating as a recurrent neural network trained through machine learning in advance so as to output (page 294, right col., , 2- This type of stacked LSTM has the capability to learn at various time scales over the given sequence of inputs. In this, the given input sequence passes through multiple non-linear recurrent hidden layers, with a large number of non-linear operations in each time step; page 293-294-we use IHR measurements for training a LSTM-RNN deep learning algorithm. The trained model is then used for testing IHR data of patients with sleep apnea and multiple control groups).
Applicant respectfully disagree with the above as Path does not disclose that "number of
elements of the normal variable length vector is variable" as recited in amended claims 1, 8, and 9. Path merely discloses that number of elements of the instantaneous heart rate feature vector is
fixed, as described in the last paragraph of page 294, left col. of Path.

Path (page 294, right col. 1st paragraph) discloses:
figure.

According to the disclosure of Path above, the number of elements of the instantaneous heart rate feature vector is constant number(w=60). Therefore, the number of elements of the instantaneous heart rate feature vector of Path is fixed not variable.

Furthermore, Path does not disclose that "each of elements of the normal variable length vector is the normal RRJ value" and "determining whether each of the RRI data is a normal RRI value or an abnormal RRI value based on comparison," as recited in amended claim 1 and similarly in amended claims 8 and 9.
Further, Path does not disclose that an abnormal variable length vector including the abnormal RRI value is not inputted to the recurrent neural network, while a normal variable
length vector is inputted to the recurrent neural network, and the normal variable length vector does not include the abnormal RRI value.

According to office Action page 10 lines 12-15, Path (page 294, right col, 2nd paragraph) disclose that "[T]his type of stacked LSTM has the capability to learn at various time scales over the given sequence of inputs. In this, the given input sequence passes through multiple non-linear recurrent hidden layer, with a large number of non-linear operations in each step."
However, this disclosure of Path, as its title (B. LSTM-RNN Network topologies)

suggests, is only concerned with the network topology, not the length of the feature vector input to the network. In Path, the length of the feature vector is disclosed in "A. Instantaneous Heart Rate Feature Vector" (page 294, left col. Last paragraph and Page 294, right col. 1st paragraph)
B. LS7M-RNN Network Topologies

For at least these reasons, claims 1, 8, and 9 are not rendered obvious by the cited references, either alone or in combination. The remaining claims depend from claim 1. Applicants submit that the dependent claims also distinguish over the cited references for the reasons provided above.
Based on these patentable distinctions, Applicants respectfully request that the obviousness rejections be withdrawn.

The claims of the application are accordingly submitted to be in condition for allowance, and passage to issue is respectfully requested. However, should the Examiner have any questions or comments which would expedite prosecution, he/she is cordially invited to telephone the undersigned at the number below.
